subjects.label: Endings and the point of no return
subjects.description: The endings themselves and the run-up to them: no happy endings, which route unlocks which ending, whether the point of no return has been reached yet and what is left to do after the credits; not the plot or characters in general.

subjects.label: Promises, hype and cut content
subjects.description: The gap between what was marketed and what shipped: content visibly cut, lifepaths and augmentations that do less than promised, the freedom the marketing sold, free DLC that never came and a launch that should have waited after years of development; not ordinary patch notes.

subjects.label: The game then and now
subjects.description: Judging the game twice, at launch and after the big patches such as 1.5 and 2.0: revised scores, an update the size of a whole game, bugs finally fixed and the long wait for a passing grade; not complaints about what was cut.

subjects.label: Your graphics card
subjects.description: Naming the card or rig it runs on and whether it is enough, from an old 1060 or 1050 Ti to a 4090, regret over not buying a bigger card, ray tracing as the showcase and needing a powerful PC; not frame-rate complaints on their own.

subjects.label: The Edgerunners anime
subjects.description: The tie-in anime and coming to the game from it: David and Lucy, whether to watch it before or after buying, and the grief it left behind; not the game's own story.

subjects.label: The cast and romances
subjects.description: Reviews built around one named character: Johnny Silverhand and Keanu Reeves in your head, Panam as a romance, Jackie, Adam Smasher as the boss to kill, Songbird; not the plot as a whole.

subjects.label: Night City as a place
subjects.description: The city itself as somewhere to live: how it feels to inhabit, its legends and its Afterlife, and where it is empty or hollow inside; not the graphics or the plot.

subjects.label: NPC behaviour and jank
subjects.description: What the people in the world do: crowd AI, NPCs stuck in T-pose or walking through solid objects, ragdoll backflips and wheelchair users running away from a gun; not crashes or lost saves.

subjects.label: Builds and cyberware
subjects.description: Character builds and implants: katana builds, Sandevistan cooldowns, remaking yourself into a cyborg, calling the doctor for implants, and augmentations that fail to change how you look; not combat mechanics in general.

subjects.label: Themes of technology and capitalism
subjects.description: What the game says about the world: anti-capitalism, the dilemmas of technology in daily life, brain chips as a coming future and the idea that nobody is innocent; not the plot or the characters.
